title.en: Coupez: a verb can be an instruction

summary.en: Notice when the subject pronoun disappears.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 5.

A director calls *Coupez!* in episode 5. The verb is an instruction, so it does not need an explicit *vous* before it. French commands often begin directly with the verb.

An instruction can address a familiar person, a group, or someone using polite address. The form helps identify which pattern is used, but tone and context still decide whether the line sounds helpful, urgent or sharp.

Pronouns can attach after an affirmative command with hyphens. Other instructions elsewhere in the season show this compact pattern. Do not assume a hyphen means a new dictionary headword: it may join a command to a pronoun.

On replay, ask who is being told to act and what action is requested. Then notice the missing subject pronoun. A short command can be a complete utterance without an extra word corresponding to English “you”.
